commands.name: folder_open
commands.description: Opens a folder in VS Code with File > Open Folder….

args.name: path
args.meaning: The folder, an absolute path or one starting with ~.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": VS Code's command-line tool is a shell command, so it isn't offered as a mode.

example_requests: Open my project folder in VS Code
Show this folder in VS Code
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: VS Code's window shows the folder; nothing on disk changes.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the change wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: another app came to the front; nothing more was done

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: nothing is at the path; nothing is done

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: VSCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it; nothing is done

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with VS Code 1.105.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
Only touches what VSCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT allows if it is set.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
VS Code is asked to show its window to Accessibility, which turns on its Screen Reader Optimized mode while it runs.
VS Code's "Do you trust the authors of the files in this folder?" is answered No, so the folder opens in Restricted Mode.
Whether it opened was read from the window title, which isn't independent of VS Code.

commands.name: file_new
commands.description: Makes a new file with text at a path that doesn't exist (File > New Text File, then Save As…); it stays open.

args.name: path
args.meaning: A new file's path, an absolute path or one starting with ~; its folder must exist.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": VS Code's command-line tool is a shell command, so it isn't offered as a mode.

example_requests: Create a new JavaScript file called app.js
Make a notes.md with this text
Start a new file in the project
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: The file holds exactly the text.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the change wasn't seen in time

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: another app came to the front; nothing more was done

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: nothing is at the path; nothing is done

errors.name: AlreadyExists
errors.when: the path is taken; nothing is overwritten

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: VSCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it; nothing is done

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with VS Code 1.105.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
Only touches what VSCODE_ALLOWED_ROOT allows if it is set.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
The text is pasted through the clipboard, which is restored afterwards; VS Code's own formatting on paste was off.
Whether the pasted text landed is judged from the window title only; if the paste is lost (say, a VS Code dialog takes it), the new file is saved empty and UIError is raised, leaving that empty file.
